checklistGeneric: Loss notice recorded in the system of record before the interaction ends
Acknowledgment timestamp captured and visible on the claim
Handler identity stamped on the intake record
checklistSpecific: Confirm the intake channel (phone, self-service portal, mobile app, EDI/agent feed) is selected on the FNOL wizard channel field
Verify the acknowledgment was issued within the 4-hour FNOL acknowledgment window measured from notice receipt, not from claim creation
For EDI/agent-feed notices, confirm the inbound transaction reference number is stored on the claim so the broker submission can be reconciled
Check that the acknowledgment text states the claim number, the assigned handling unit, and what the insured must do next
Confirm the acknowledgment was delivered on the channel the insured elected (SMS/email/portal message) and the delivery status is Sent, not Queued or Failed

testing.expected: Acknowledgment timestamp exists and is within 4 hours of the notice receipt time
No FNOL record sits in Draft/unacknowledged status past the 4-hour SLA

checklistGeneric: CAT code applied only from the approved active-event list
Coding action written to the claim audit trail
checklistSpecific: Confirm the CAT event code selected matches an event whose status is Active and whose date window covers the reported loss date
Verify the loss location falls inside the declared CAT geography (state/county/ZIP band) before applying the code
Check that the PCS/event catalogue number is populated on the CAT event field, not a free-text description
Confirm the claim reserve category flips to the CAT bucket so event aggregation picks it up on the next roll-up
Where the loss is inside the window but outside the peril (e.g. a non-wind loss during a hurricane CAT), confirm the code was NOT applied and the reason is noted

testing.expected: An active CAT event code with a matching event date window is set on the claim
No claim carries a CAT code for an event that is Closed or Cancelled

checklistGeneric: Identity verification outcome recorded before any policy detail is disclosed
Failed verification attempts logged with the reason
checklistSpecific: Confirm at least two identifiers were matched against the policy record (named insured, policy number, address, date of birth or last four of the payment method)
Verify the caller relationship is captured as insured, additional insured, driver, agent/broker, or third-party claimant, and that third parties are not given insured-only policy detail
For agent or broker submissions, confirm the producer code on the notice matches the producer of record on the policy
Where verification fails, confirm the intake continues as an unverified third-party notice with restricted disclosure rather than being abandoned
Check the verification result flag is set on the claim contact record, not just noted in the free-text call summary

testing.expected: Verification status and relationship-to-insured are populated on the reporting party
No coverage limits or policy financials disclosed on a notice where verification status is Failed

checklistGeneric: Claim number issued from the system sequence, never hand-written or reused
Communication of the number recorded on the claim
checklistSpecific: Read the full claim number back to the reporting party and confirm they repeat it correctly before ending the call
Confirm the claim number was also pushed to the insured in writing on their elected channel (SMS/email/portal) so it is not phone-only
Verify the number issued is the ClaimCenter claim number and not the internal exposure or activity id
Check the claims service phone number and hours are given alongside the claim number
Where the notice was matched to an existing claim, confirm the pre-existing claim number was quoted rather than a new one created

testing.expected: A system-generated claim number exists and is referenced in the outbound acknowledgment

testing.location: Claim search by policy and loss date
testing.expected: No duplicate claim number issued for the same policy, loss date and loss location

checklistGeneric: Notification record created in the system of record, not held in a spreadsheet or inbox
All mandatory intake fields completed before submission
checklistSpecific: Confirm the policy number, named insured, loss date and loss description are populated on the new loss record
Verify the loss date is on or after policy inception and on or before expiry, and flag the notice if it is not
Check the line of business and coverage type selected match the policy the notice was written against
Confirm the FNOL record is submitted (status New/Open) rather than left in Draft at the end of the interaction
Verify the reporting party contact number and preferred contact method are stored so the adjuster can make first contact

testing.expected: Claim exists in Open status with policy number, loss date and loss description populated
No FNOL left in Draft status beyond end of shift

checklistGeneric: Metadata written by the system clock, not typed by the handler
Channel value chosen from the controlled list
checklistSpecific: Confirm the notice received date/time is stamped from the inbound event (call connect, portal submit, EDI receipt), not the time the handler finished keying
Verify the reported-to-company date drives the acknowledgment and contact SLA clocks on the claim
Check the channel field is one of the controlled values (Phone, Portal, Mobile App, EDI/Agent, Email) with no free text
For after-hours or overflow vendor intake, confirm the original vendor receipt time is carried across rather than the time of re-key next morning
Confirm time zone is stored consistently with the loss location so late-night losses are not shifted a day

testing.location: Claim > Loss Details > Reported date and Reported by channel
testing.expected: Reported date/time and channel are populated from system capture
No claim where the reported date/time is later than the claim creation timestamp

checklistGeneric: Duplicate search performed before any new claim is created
Match or create decision recorded on the claim
checklistSpecific: Run the duplicate search on policy number plus loss date range before pressing Create, and record the search result
Where a matching claim exists, add the new information as an exposure or note on that claim rather than opening a second claim number
Confirm a genuinely new event on the same policy within the same week is opened as a separate claim with the differing loss date and cause noted
For multi-vehicle or multi-claimant losses, verify one claim is created with separate exposures per claimant, not one claim per caller
Check any duplicate opened in error is closed as Duplicate and cross-referenced to the surviving claim number

testing.expected: Either a link to the matched existing claim or a documented no-match search result exists

testing.location: Claim list by policy and loss date
testing.expected: No two open claims share the same policy, loss date and loss cause

checklistGeneric: Queue position reviewed against the published service level at a fixed cadence
Every reassignment recorded with the reason
checklistSpecific: Check the oldest waiting item in each intake queue (phone, portal, email, EDI) against its SLA clock and act on any item past 75% of the window first
Move handlers between voice and back-office intake queues using the skill routing profile rather than assigning claims by hand
Confirm portal and EDI notices are not left ageing behind voice traffic when phone volume spikes
Verify overflow to the after-hours or BPO intake vendor is triggered before abandonment breaches the 5% threshold, not after
Record the rebalance action and volumes in the shift handover so the next supervisor inherits the picture

testing.expected: Each intake queue shows a longest-wait value within its published SLA
No unassigned FNOL older than the intake SLA at end of shift

checklistGeneric: Routing driven by the configured rule set, not manual pick-up
Routing outcome visible on the claim
checklistSpecific: Confirm every claim carrying the active CAT code lands in the CAT surge queue rather than the standard territory queue
Verify the CAT adjuster pool assignment respects state adjuster licensing and emergency-licence status for the affected states
Check that life-safety and habitability cases (fire loss, uninhabitable dwelling, injury) are pulled to the priority CAT lane ahead of routine property damage
Confirm commercial and large-account CAT claims are routed to the large-loss CAT lane, not the personal-lines surge pool
Verify any claim that fails CAT routing lands in the exception queue with an owner rather than sitting unassigned

testing.expected: CAT-coded claims are assigned to the CAT surge group with a named adjuster
No CAT-coded claim remains in a non-CAT queue after the routing run

checklistGeneric: Acknowledgment generated from the approved template version
Send status confirmed, not assumed
checklistSpecific: Confirm the acknowledgment template merges the claim number, loss date, assigned unit and the claims contact number without leaving unresolved merge tokens
Verify next steps are stated concretely (who will call, by when, what documents to gather) rather than a generic thank-you
Check the send channel matches the insured recorded preference and that email/SMS delivery status is Sent or Delivered
Confirm no coverage position, liability view or settlement expectation is implied anywhere in the acknowledgment text
Where delivery bounces, verify a retry on the alternate channel is raised as an activity rather than the failure being closed silently

testing.expected: An acknowledgment document exists with status Sent and the claim number in the body
No acknowledgment containing unresolved merge fields or a coverage opinion

checklistGeneric: Minimum data set validated before the notice is released to assignment
Gaps raised as a follow-up activity with an owner and due date
checklistSpecific: Confirm the reporter has authority to report: named insured, additional insured, driver on the policy, producer of record, or an authorised representative with documented consent
Verify the minimum notice set is present: policy number, loss date, loss location, loss cause and a callable contact number
Check the policy status on the loss date is In Force and not cancelled, lapsed or not-taken-up
Where a third party reports the loss, confirm the insured is still contacted independently rather than relying on the third-party account
Confirm incomplete notices are still logged and assigned with an information-request activity, never rejected at the door

testing.expected: All mandatory FNOL validations pass or an open information-request activity exists for each gap
No claim advanced to assignment where the policy was not in force on the loss date without a coverage-question flag

checklistGeneric: Every attachment indexed to a document type, never left untyped
Source and date of receipt recorded for each item
checklistSpecific: Confirm photographs and video are attached to the claim file itself rather than left in the intake mailbox or the agent email thread
Verify each attachment is tagged with the correct document type (loss photo, police report, estimate, receipt, medical bill) so downstream searches find it
Check that the correct exposure is selected when the claim has multiple claimants, so third-party evidence is not filed under the insured exposure
Confirm upload of large media from the self-service portal completed (no partial or zero-byte files) and the insured sees the item listed on their portal claim view
Verify sensitive items such as medical records or identity documents are filed to the restricted-access document class

testing.expected: At least one typed, indexed evidence document is linked to the claim and to the correct exposure
No zero-byte or untyped attachments on the claim

checklistGeneric: Structured date/time/location fields used rather than narrative text
Unknown values explicitly marked unknown, not left blank
checklistSpecific: Confirm the loss date and time are entered as discrete values and that the time of day is captured, not defaulted to midnight
Verify the loss address is validated against the address service and resolves to a rooftop or street-level match, not just a city centroid
For mobile or portal FNOL, check the captured GPS coordinates fall within a sensible distance of the entered street address and query the gap if not
Confirm the loss location is distinguished from the risk address on the policy when the loss happened away from the insured premises
Where the loss date is a range (e.g. theft discovered later), verify both the date of occurrence and date of discovery are captured

testing.expected: Loss date, loss time and a validated loss location (with coordinates where captured) are populated
No claim with a loss location left blank or set only to the policy risk address by default

checklistGeneric: Questionnaire completed in the guided flow rather than free-text notes
All conditional branches answered to the end
checklistSpecific: Confirm the questionnaire version selected matches the line of business and loss cause (auto collision, property water, liability bodily injury are different scripts)
Verify every conditional branch triggered by the answers has been completed, with no half-finished sub-sections
Check that answers driving downstream automation (injury yes/no, vehicle drivable, property habitable, third party involved) are set explicitly rather than left null
Confirm free-text is used only for the narrative and that facts captured in structured fields are not re-typed inconsistently in the notes
Verify the questionnaire is saved against the claim so the adjuster sees the same answer set the insured gave at intake

testing.expected: A completed questionnaire matching the line of business and loss cause is attached to the claim
No mandatory questionnaire item left unanswered on a submitted FNOL

checklistGeneric: Estimate captured as the reporting party stated it, with the source noted
No coverage or settlement commitment given while capturing detail
checklistSpecific: Record the damaged property description in enough detail to size the loss: building versus contents, rooms affected, vehicle make/model/year, mileage and drivability
Capture the insured own rough estimate of the loss value and mark it clearly as an unverified insured estimate, not a reserve figure
Confirm whether the property is currently habitable or the vehicle drivable, as this drives emergency mitigation and rental/ALE decisions
Note any emergency repairs already carried out or in progress and ask the insured to retain receipts and damaged materials
Check whether other insurance or a warranty may respond so potential other-carrier involvement is flagged at intake

testing.expected: Damaged item description and an initial loss estimate with its source are recorded
No statement of coverage or payable amount recorded during detail capture

checklistGeneric: Each party added as a structured contact with a defined role
Contact detail captured well enough to reach the party without a follow-up call
checklistSpecific: Add each involved party as its own contact record with the role set (claimant, driver, passenger, witness, third-party insurer, property owner, repairer)
Capture the other party carrier name, policy number and claim number where a third-party vehicle or property is involved, since this drives subrogation
Record injuries reported by any party, including whether an ambulance attended or treatment was sought, on the injured party record
Confirm minors and vulnerable parties are recorded with the responsible adult contact rather than a direct contact number
Verify witness contact details are captured while the reporting party still has them to hand, not deferred to the adjuster call

testing.expected: Every party mentioned in the loss narrative exists as a typed contact with a role and reachable contact detail
No involved party recorded only in free-text notes without a contact record

checklistGeneric: State-driven field set applied from the loss jurisdiction, not the policy mailing state
Completion validated before the claim leaves intake
checklistSpecific: Confirm the jurisdiction driving the mandatory field set is derived from the loss location and the policy issuing state, and that the resolved state is visible on the claim
Complete state-specific reportable fields such as injury/fatality indicators, uninsured-motorist involvement and total-loss indicators required for statistical reporting
Verify no-fault and PIP states have the additional injury and medical-provider fields populated where an injury is reported
Check the state-mandated acknowledgment and contact clocks configured for the jurisdiction are attached to the claim rather than the generic default
Confirm any state field left blank is because it is genuinely not applicable, and that the not-applicable reason is recorded

testing.expected: All jurisdiction-mandated FNOL fields for the resolved loss state are populated
No claim released from intake with an unresolved mandatory state field error

checklistGeneric: Narrative recorded in the insured own words without handler interpretation
Loss cause selected from the controlled cause-of-loss list
checklistSpecific: Select the cause of loss from the controlled list (wind, water non-weather, fire, theft, collision, liability slip/fall) and make sure it matches the narrative rather than defaulting to Other
Record the sequence of events in order: what happened first, what failed, what damage followed, so proximate cause can be assessed later
Capture facts that bear on coverage without arguing them: how long water had been leaking, whether the property was vacant, whether the vehicle was in business use
Keep the narrative factual and avoid recording the handler own opinion on liability or coverage
Confirm the narrative length and detail are sufficient that the adjuster can prepare the first contact without re-interviewing from scratch

testing.location: Claim > Loss Details > Cause of loss and description
testing.expected: A controlled cause-of-loss value and a sequenced narrative description are recorded
No claim with cause of loss set to Other or Unknown without an explanatory note

checklistGeneric: Reference numbers stored in dedicated fields, not buried in notes
Issuing agency captured alongside every reference number
checklistSpecific: Capture the police or fire report number together with the issuing agency name and jurisdiction, since the number alone is not orderable
Where no report was filed, record explicitly that no report exists and why, rather than leaving the field blank
For theft, arson and injury losses, confirm a report number is pursued as a follow-up activity if not available at intake
Record the ambulance or hospital reference where emergency services attended an injury
Verify the report reference is placed on the claim so the report-ordering task can be raised without a call back to the insured

testing.location: Claim > Loss Details > Official report fields
testing.expected: Report number and issuing agency are recorded, or an explicit no-report-filed value is set
No theft or fire claim without either a report reference or an open activity to obtain one

checklistGeneric: Completeness check run against the published intake data standard
Each identified gap raised as an owned activity with a due date
checklistSpecific: Cross-check the structured fields against the narrative: loss date, loss location and party count must agree with what the description says happened
Confirm the reported loss cause is consistent with the coverage and line of business selected, and query mismatches before assignment
Verify injury and third-party indicators are consistent with the contact records actually created on the claim
Check the intake record against the FNOL quality scorecard criteria and log the score so intake quality is trended, not just fixed silently
Raise each remaining gap as a follow-up activity assigned to a named handler with a due date rather than a general note

testing.expected: An intake validation activity is completed and any gaps have owned follow-up activities
No inconsistency between the injury/third-party indicators and the contacts recorded on the claim

checklistGeneric: Assignment produced by the configured rule set rather than manual selection
Rule outcome and any override recorded on the claim
checklistSpecific: Confirm the assignment rule evaluated line of business, loss state/territory and complexity tier together, not just territory
Verify the selected handler holds an active adjuster licence for the loss jurisdiction and has authority for the assigned tier
Check claims above the senior-adjuster threshold are not routed to a general handler by the rule
Where the rule is overridden manually, confirm the reason is recorded and the override is visible to the supervisor
Confirm the rule outcome names an individual handler, not just a group, before the assignment SLA expires

testing.expected: Assignment shows the rule that fired and a named licensed handler
No claim sitting on group-only assignment past the 24-hour assignment standard

checklistGeneric: Flags applied from the controlled flag list with a documented trigger
Flag changes written to the claim audit trail
checklistSpecific: Apply the catastrophe flag only where the loss matches a declared event by date, geography and peril
Set the major-account flag where the policy belongs to a named large or strategic account so account-level service protocols engage
Apply the mass-tort or aggregation flag where the loss shares a common defect, product or event with other open claims
Confirm flags that change reserving or reporting treatment are recorded with the reason, since they feed aggregate and reinsurance views
Verify a flag applied in error is removed with a reason rather than left on the claim

testing.expected: Applicable severity flags are set with a recorded trigger reason
No flag added or removed without an accompanying audit entry

checklistGeneric: Severity assessed against the published triage criteria, not handler judgement alone
Assigned tier recorded with a short written rationale
checklistSpecific: Score the claim against the triage criteria: injury severity, number of claimants, estimated damage value, coverage question and litigation likelihood
Compare the estimated exposure against the reserve benchmark table for the line of business before setting the tier
Escalate the tier where a coverage question, a fatality, a commercial third party or an attorney is already involved, regardless of the damage estimate
Confirm the assigned tier drives the handling track and adjuster authority level, and that a mismatch is corrected rather than worked around
Record the rationale in the triage note so a later file review can see why the tier was chosen

testing.expected: A severity tier is set with a triage rationale note referencing the criteria used
No claim above the large-loss threshold carrying a low-severity tier without documented approval

checklistGeneric: Assignment made to a named individual within the assignment SLA
Licence and authority validated before the assignment is confirmed
checklistSpecific: Verify the adjuster licence for the loss state is active and unexpired on the assignment date, including any emergency CAT licence
Confirm the adjuster line-of-business authority covers the claim type (property, auto physical damage, bodily injury, commercial)
Check the assignment respects the settlement-authority ladder so the reserve estimate does not exceed the handler authority
Confirm the assignment was made within 24 hours of the notice and that the claim did not sit in a group queue overnight
Verify current workload and absence status were considered so the claim is not assigned to a handler on leave

testing.expected: A named adjuster with an active state licence and adequate authority is assigned within 24 hours
No claim assigned to a handler without an active licence in the loss jurisdiction

checklistGeneric: Handling instructions issued from the approved template for the claim type
Receipt by the assigned handler confirmed, not assumed
checklistSpecific: Confirm the handling-instruction package attached to the claim covers coverage position to date, contact SLA, diary cadence and reserve expectations
Verify special account or programme instructions (large account service standards, TPA protocols, litigation handling rules) are included where applicable
Check the package names the escalation contact and the authority limits that apply to this claim
Confirm the assigned adjuster has acknowledged the assignment activity rather than the package merely being generated
Verify the package version matches the current published handling guideline, not a superseded copy

testing.expected: A current-version handling-instruction package is attached and its acknowledgment activity is complete
No assignment activity left unacknowledged by the assigned handler

checklistGeneric: Mitigation decision made and recorded at first review, not deferred
Vendor instruction issued from the approved network
checklistSpecific: Ask directly whether the property is secure, dry and habitable and whether anyone has been displaced, and record the answers
Where emergency services are required, dispatch board-up, water extraction or tarping from the approved vendor network within the same working day
Confirm emergency accommodation or a hire vehicle is authorised where the insured cannot occupy the property or drive, and record the authorised duration and rate
Advise the insured to mitigate further damage and retain receipts and damaged items, and note that advice on the claim
Where mitigation is not needed, record the explicit not-required decision with the reason rather than leaving the question unanswered

testing.expected: A recorded mitigation decision exists, with a vendor assignment where services were required
No claim flagged uninhabitable or undrivable without a mitigation or accommodation decision

checklistGeneric: Decision documented in the claim file within 24 hours of being made
Author and timestamp captured automatically on the note
checklistSpecific: Record the triage note as a typed note category (Triage decision) so it is retrievable, not as a generic file note
State the severity tier chosen, the criteria that drove it and the handling track the claim was routed to
Document any deviation from the rule-based outcome and who approved the deviation
Confirm the note is written on the claim rather than in an email thread or the assignment spreadsheet
Verify the note is legible to a reviewer with no prior knowledge of the call, including what is still unknown

testing.expected: A typed triage decision note exists within 24 hours of the triage action
No triage decision recorded only outside the claim system

checklistGeneric: Notification issued within the contact standard and logged on the claim
Each contact attempt recorded, whether or not it connected
checklistSpecific: Confirm the insured was told the handler name, direct phone number, email and working hours within 24 hours of assignment
Verify the notification also states what happens next and the expected timescale for the first substantive contact
Where the insured is not reached, confirm the attempt is logged and a second attempt on an alternate channel is diarised, not just left
Check the agent or broker of record is copied where the account service model requires it
Confirm the handler details are also visible on the insured self-service portal claim view, not only in the phone call

testing.expected: A logged notification of the assigned handler exists within 24 hours of assignment
No assigned claim older than 24 hours with zero recorded contact attempts

checklistGeneric: Screening completed on every notice, not only on suspicious ones
Screening outcome recorded even where no indicator is found
checklistSpecific: Run the documented red-flag checklist against the FNOL: loss shortly after inception or after a coverage increase, no police report on a theft, prior similar claims, reluctance to give detail, pressure for a fast cash settlement
Confirm the automated fraud score from the detection engine has returned and been reviewed, rather than the claim advancing before scoring completes
Check the sanctions and watchlist screening of the named parties has run at first notice and that any hit is escalated before any payment step
Where indicators are present, confirm the SIU referral is raised within 48 hours with the specific indicators cited, not a generic suspicion
Verify the insured was not told they are under fraud review and that the claim continues to be handled normally while screening proceeds

testing.location: Claim > Fraud score and indicator list
testing.expected: A completed fraud screening result with the red-flag checklist outcome is recorded on the claim
No claim with triggered red flags lacking an SIU referral beyond 48 hours

checklistGeneric: Diary dates set at assignment, not at first review
Every diary has a named owner
checklistSpecific: Set the first contact diary to fall inside the 24-hour insured contact standard rather than at the end of the week
Set the coverage confirmation diary within the 24-hour post-assignment coverage standard
Set reserve review diaries at 30, 60 and 90 days in line with the reserve review cadence
Confirm the diary cadence matches the severity tier, with tighter intervals on large-loss and litigated claims
Verify diaries are owned by the assigned handler and reassign automatically on handler change rather than going orphan

testing.expected: Contact, coverage and 30/60/90-day reserve review diaries exist with a named owner
No open claim without a future-dated diary entry

checklistGeneric: Reserve posted within the initial reserve standard window
Written rationale recorded alongside every reserve figure
checklistSpecific: Post the initial indemnity reserve using the reserve worksheet for the severity tier and line of business rather than a round-number placeholder
Set expense reserves separately from indemnity, including anticipated adjuster, expert and legal costs
Confirm reserves are posted per exposure where the claim has multiple claimants, not as a single lump on the claim
Verify the initial reserve is posted within 72 hours of the notice and that the reserve rationale note cites the benchmark or estimate used
Where the reserve exceeds the handler authority or the $25K change threshold, confirm manager approval is captured before posting

testing.expected: Indemnity and expense reserves are posted per exposure within 72 hours with a rationale note
No reserve above the authority threshold posted without recorded manager approval

checklistGeneric: Routing executed by the published rule set with a version reference
Routing result recorded on the claim audit trail
checklistSpecific: Confirm the routing rule set version in force is the current published one and note it on the routing result
Verify the claim landed on the correct handling track: fast-track low-complexity, standard, complex/large-loss, litigation or CAT
Check that fast-track eligibility criteria (no injury, single party, damage under threshold, no coverage question) are all satisfied before a claim is fast-tracked
Confirm specialty triggers (bodily injury, commercial liability, subrogation potential, total loss) redirect the claim before it reaches a generalist queue
Verify a claim that matches no rule lands in the routing exception queue with an owner rather than defaulting to an arbitrary group

testing.expected: The routing rule that fired and the resulting handling track are recorded on the claim
No claim in the routing exception queue without an assigned owner

checklistGeneric: Assignment made from the CAT roster in force for the declared event
CAT management oversight recorded on the assignment
checklistSpecific: Assign only from the CAT adjuster roster activated for this event, including approved independent adjuster firms
Verify each assigned CAT adjuster holds a valid or emergency licence for the affected state before the first field visit
Confirm the CAT team lead is set as the supervisory contact on the claim so oversight is visible on the file
Balance assignments by geographic cluster so field routing is efficient rather than assigning by simple round-robin
Confirm complex or large-loss CAT claims are steered to the large-loss CAT lane rather than a general CAT handler

testing.expected: CAT claims are assigned to a rostered CAT adjuster with a named CAT supervisor
No CAT claim assigned to a handler outside the activated CAT roster

checklistGeneric: Rationale recorded at the time of the decision, not reconstructed later
Audit trail entry links the decision to the person who made it
checklistSpecific: Record why the claim went to the track it did, referencing the specific trigger (injury reported, reserve above threshold, coverage question, attorney involvement)
Where the automated routing was overridden, document what the rule proposed, what was chosen instead and who authorised the change
Confirm escalation rationale names the receiving role or unit and what decision is being asked of them
Verify the rationale is written on the claim audit trail rather than in a routing spreadsheet or chat message
Check that a reviewer with no prior knowledge could follow the routing history end to end from the audit trail alone

testing.expected: Each routing and escalation event carries a rationale entry with an author and timestamp
No manual routing override recorded without a documented reason and approver

checklistGeneric: Escalation triggered against published thresholds, not personal judgement
Receiving reviewer acknowledges the escalation
checklistSpecific: Escalate where the incurred or estimated exposure crosses the large-loss threshold, and re-check after every reserve movement rather than only at intake
Confirm claims above $100K are moved to a senior adjuster and claims above $500K are placed under claims management oversight
Include the key facts, coverage position, current reserve and the specific decision being sought in the escalation summary
Verify the escalation is acknowledged by the receiving senior handler or manager within the escalation window, not just sent
Where the escalation is declined, confirm the reason and the agreed handling plan are recorded on the claim

testing.expected: An escalation record exists with the trigger threshold cited and an acknowledgment from the receiving reviewer
No claim above the large-loss threshold without a completed escalation

checklistGeneric: Litigation flag applied against published thresholds and triggers
Legal unit notified through the standard channel with the file accessible
checklistSpecific: Flag the claim where any litigation trigger is present: attorney representation notified, suit papers served, a demand letter received, or a fatality/serious injury
Record the date of service or date the demand was received, since response deadlines run from it and are not extendable
Confirm the notification to the legal unit includes the coverage position, current reserve and the response deadline
Verify the reserve has been reviewed for legal exposure and defence costs at the point of flagging, not left at the pre-litigation level
Check defence counsel, where instructed, comes from the approved panel and the instruction is recorded on the claim

testing.expected: Litigation flag is set with the trigger date and a legal notification activity recorded
No served suit or attorney representation on file without a litigation flag and legal notification

checklistGeneric: Task list generated automatically on assignment, not built by hand
Every generated task has an owner and a due date
checklistSpecific: Confirm the generated task list matches the claim type and severity tier rather than a single generic list for all claims
Verify the customer contact SLA task is dated to the 24-hour insured contact standard measured from assignment
Check coverage verification, reserve setting and evidence collection tasks are all present with due dates inside their respective standards
Confirm state-specific contact and acknowledgment deadlines for the loss jurisdiction override the generic default where they are shorter
Verify the tasks and SLA clocks are attached to the claim so they surface on the adjuster diary, not just in the routing engine

testing.expected: A generated intake task list with owners and SLA-derived due dates is attached to the claim
No generated task without a due date or an owner

checklistGeneric: Exception monitoring run on a defined cadence with a named owner
Every identified exception logged rather than fixed silently
checklistSpecific: Review the routing exception queue at least daily and age each item against the assignment standard
Identify claims that fell through to a default group because no rule matched, and record the rule gap for configuration fix
Flag claims routed to a handler without the required licence or authority for the loss jurisdiction
Spot claims with a specialty trigger (injury, litigation, subrogation, total loss) sitting on a generalist track
Trend recurring exception causes so the routing rule set is corrected rather than the same claims being fixed by hand each day

testing.expected: A dated exception review exists listing each exception with its cause and owner
No exception older than the assignment SLA left unreviewed

checklistGeneric: Reassignment made to a handler with the correct licence and authority
Reason for the misroute recorded on the claim
checklistSpecific: Confirm the claim is reassigned to the correct handling track and a named handler, not simply pushed back to an unassigned queue
Verify the SLA clocks are recalculated from the original notice date so a misroute does not reset the insured contact deadline
Check the outgoing handler has recorded what was already done (contacts made, reserves posted, documents requested) before the handover
Confirm the insured is told of the handler change where contact had already been made in their name
Record the misroute cause so the routing rule or data-quality gap can be corrected upstream

testing.expected: A reassignment entry exists with the misroute reason and the corrected handling track
No reassigned claim whose insured contact SLA was reset to the reassignment date

checklistGeneric: Specialty routing applied as soon as the injury indicator is set
Assignment recorded to a named specialist, not a group
checklistSpecific: Route to a bodily-injury specialist as soon as any injury is reported, before medical detail is complete, rather than waiting for bills
Confirm serious-injury markers (fatality, hospitalisation, spinal or head injury, minor claimant) push the claim to the senior BI or complex lane
Verify a structured-settlement consultant is engaged where the exposure profile and claimant circumstances warrant it, and the engagement is recorded
Check medical management or nurse case review is triggered where treatment is ongoing, and that the referral is on the claim
Confirm the BI reserve is set on the injury exposure separately from property damage on the same claim

testing.expected: Injury exposures are assigned to a named bodily-injury specialist with a separate reserve
No injury-flagged claim left on a property-damage-only handler

checklistGeneric: Escalation diaries set at the point of escalation, not later
